basis: Skeletal dysplasia, heart defects and developmental impairment define it; cleft palate occurs in 30-79%. Hair/skin abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart defects are defining features; pulmonic stenosis is annotated in 80-99%.
decisions.neurologic: primary: developmental impairment is a defining feature, with cognitive impairment annotated in 80-99%.

basis: Loose anagen hair, developmental disability and heart defects characterize it; ptosis 24/33 and strabismus 15/30 support ocular involvement. Common skeletal findings omitted at the cap.

decisions.ocular: involved: ptosis occurs in 24/33 and strabismus in 15/30; persistent eyelid and ocular motor dysfunction merit the fourth axis.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: joint hypermobility (5/5) and sternal anomalies (17/32) qualify less strongly by severity than ocular dysfunction and are omitted at the four-axis cap.

basis: Inherited microcytic anemia with intrinsic iron-handling defects and iron overload; common hepatic or cardiac functional injury is not established across the umbrella.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this inherited anemia group includes intrinsic disorders of iron transport/utilization; the metabolic defect is part of the disease, rather than treatment-induced overload.

basis: Chronic arachnoid inflammation; hearing and visual impairment are each annotated in 80-99%. Generic arachnoiditis includes noninfectious, nonautoimmune causes.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: arachnoiditis may follow chemical or mechanical injury as well as infection; inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease.

basis: Pineal parenchymal neoplasm arises in CNS tissue and an endocrine gland; endocrine-gland origin qualifies without requiring hormone dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the pineal is an endocrine gland, and this tumor arises from its parenchymal cells; the gland-disease rule does not require hormone dysfunction.

basis: Motor-neuron loss and progressive skeletal muscle atrophy define SMA across subtypes. Respiratory muscle weakness does not itself establish direct lung damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal muscle atrophy is named and explicitly defining, not merely an optional complication; denervation explains its mechanism without changing its defining status.

basis: Severe infantile motor-neuron degeneration with defining progressive muscle weakness and atrophy; respiratory failure reflects muscle denervation rather than primary lung damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: severe progressive skeletal muscle weakness and atrophy define this SMA subtype and occur in essentially all patients.

basis: Zellweger-spectrum metabolic disease; neurologic impairment, hepatopathy and sensorineural hearing loss each commonly exceed 30%. Common retinal disease omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.ocular: none: retinal disease commonly exceeds 30%, but neurologic disease, hepatopathy and very frequent hearing loss take the three available involved slots.
decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing loss affects most Zellweger-spectrum patients, exceeding 30%; prioritized over retinal disease at the four-axis cap.

basis: Contractures, severe CNS dysfunction and restrictive microstomia define it. Blepharophimosis is annotated in 80-99%, but functional ocular damage is not established.

decisions.ocular: none: frequent blepharophimosis describes eyelid morphology; the record does not establish impaired lid function, visual loss or other direct functional ocular damage.

basis: Marrow/blood myeloid malignancy; infant t(1;22) leukemia commonly infiltrates the liver with marked hepatomegaly (>30%), representing direct malignant occupation.

decisions.hepatic: involved: hepatic leukemic infiltration with hepatomegaly is common (>30%) in infant t(1;22) disease; direct tumor occupation qualifies even without liver failure.
